g.text: R3 debug control - the four-state machine, STOP-BEFORE landing, the opcode flows, and the bring-up trap

g.text: THE STATE ENCODING - one wire, and R2's old 0/1 keep their meaning

g.data-qualified-name: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes. or the strap. or reset
g.text: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes, or the strap, or reset

g.data-qualified-name: STOP-BEFORE - the hit compares the LANDING address. not the current one
g.text: STOP-BEFORE - the hit compares the LANDING address, not the current one

g.data-qualified-name: THE FOUR OPCODE FLOWS - TARGET_HOST only. the loopback target answers UNSUPPORTED
g.text: THE FOUR OPCODE FLOWS - TARGET_HOST only; the loopback target answers UNSUPPORTED

g.data-qualified-name: THE BRING-UP TRAP - once held. the run strap is ignored BOTH WAYS
g.text: THE BRING-UP TRAP - once held, the run strap is ignored BOTH WAYS

g.data-qualified-name: THE SUBTLETY. BP_SET clears bp_en and bp_hit but NOT dbg_hold_r
g.text: THE SUBTLETY: BP_SET clears bp_en and bp_hit but NOT dbg_hold_r

g.data-qualified-name: THE STATE ENCODING - one wire. and R2.s old 0.1 keep their meaning.enc
g.text: dbg_state = dbg_hold_r ? (bp_hit ? 3 : 2)
bp_flags = {bp_hit, bp_en}
bit0 = breakpoint ARMED
bit1 = HIT latched

g.data-qualified-name: THE STATE ENCODING - one wire. and R2.s old 0.1 keep their meaning.s0
g.text: 0 STOPPED
the normal boot stop:
run=0, no hold,
PC HELD AT 0

g.data-qualified-name: THE STATE ENCODING - one wire. and R2.s old 0.1 keep their meaning.s1
g.text: 1 RUNNING
the strap is high and
no debug hold is
asserted

g.data-qualified-name: THE STATE ENCODING - one wire. and R2.s old 0.1 keep their meaning.s2
g.text: 2 DEBUG_HOLD
held by the debug controls
with the PC PRESERVED
(single-stepping).
The core is NOT executing.

g.data-qualified-name: THE STATE ENCODING - one wire. and R2.s old 0.1 keep their meaning.s3
g.text: 3 BP_HIT
held by the breakpoint:
PC preserved,
the hit LATCHED

g.data-qualified-name: THE STATE ENCODING - one wire. and R2.s old 0.1 keep their meaning.addr
g.text: bp_addr is the armed address, or 0 when disarmed.
A BREAKPOINT AT ADDRESS 0 IS LEGAL and is told
apart from 'disarmed' by bp_flags bit0, not by
the address - which is the whole reason the flag
exists.

g.data-qualified-name: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes. or the strap. or reset.t0
g.text: 0 STOPPED

g.data-qualified-name: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes. or the strap. or reset.t1
g.text: 1 RUNNING

g.data-qualified-name: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes. or the strap. or reset.t2
g.text: 2 DEBUG_HOLD

g.data-qualified-name: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes. or the strap. or reset.t3
g.text: 3 BP_HIT

g.data-qualified-name: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes. or the strap. or reset.tclr
g.text: BP_CLR - THE ONLY RELEASE
releases the hold AND disarms.
with run=1 the core RESUMES (state 1);
with run=0 it returns to the normal boot
stop (state 0, PC re-zeroed at that same
edge). IDEMPOTENT - safe when disarmed.

g.data-qualified-name: THE MACHINE - every edge is one of the four opcodes. or the strap. or reset.tstep
g.text: DEBUG_STEP - executes EXACTLY ONE
instruction, then returns to held.
From 0 or 2. NOT_READY, with NO fault
and NO side effect, while the core is
FREE-RUNNING (run=1 and not held).

g.data-qualified-name: STOP-BEFORE - the hit compares the LANDING address. not the current one.cmp
g.text: THE COMPARISON
if (bp_en && !dbg_hold_r && (run || dbg_step)
&& (dbg_next_pc == bp_addr))
begin bp_hit <= 1; dbg_hold_r <= 1; end
dbg_next_pc is the combinational next PC - the
address the core is ABOUT to execute.

g.data-qualified-name: STOP-BEFORE - the hit compares the LANDING address. not the current one.sb
g.text: SO THE CORE IS HELD AT THAT EDGE WITH
PC == bp_addr, AND THE INSTRUCTION AT bp_addr
HAS NOT RUN. No io_we, no dmem_we, no a/x/y
effect of it occurred. That is the stop-before a
debugger expects: inspect it, then step THAT
very instruction.

g.data-qualified-name: STOP-BEFORE - the hit compares the LANDING address. not the current one.sb2
g.text: AND STOP-BEFORE IS NOT A NO-OP STEP.
Stepping 1 to 2 with the breakpoint armed at 2
DOES execute the LDI at 1 - a step retires the
instruction it stepped FROM, as a step always
does - and leaves the instruction AT 2 untouched.
It protects the one the debugger is about to
inspect, and that is the entire distinction.

g.data-qualified-name: STOP-BEFORE - the hit compares the LANDING address. not the current one.sb3
g.text: THE PC IS PRESERVED, NOT RE-ZEROED
Under a hold the PC keeps its value across
arbitrarily many cycles. Only the boot stop
(run=0, no hold) re-zeroes it, exactly as R2's
read arbitration requires.

g.data-qualified-name: STOP-BEFORE - the hit compares the LANDING address. not the current one.sb4
g.text: THE FETCH FOLLOWS THE SAME THREE MODES
imem_addr = cpu_exec ? next_pc
: dbg_hold ? pc
so each mode keeps the pipeline invariant R2's
read arbitration depends on, and insn follows the
mode rather than being imem[pc] unconditionally.

g.data-qualified-name: THE FOUR OPCODE FLOWS - TARGET_HOST only. the loopback target answers UNSUPPORTED.f_step
g.text: 0x21 DEBUG_STEP len 0
-> (OK, state, pc_next, bp_addr, bp_flags)
5 words.
state and bp_flags are the state AFTER the step:
a step that lands on the armed address reports
state 3 and flags 0x03.
bp_flags here is computed POST-step, NOT the
pre-edge latch, which would report the hit the
step is clearing.
On refusal: NOT_READY, state/pc from the live
registers, and the PRE-edge bp_flags.

g.data-qualified-name: THE FOUR OPCODE FLOWS - TARGET_HOST only. the loopback target answers UNSUPPORTED.f_set
g.text: 0x22 DEBUG_BP_SET len 1
-> (OK, state, pc, bp_addr, bp_flags)
5 words. ONE payload word: the address.
address must be < IMEM_WORDS, else RANGE, and
then the breakpoint is NOT armed and NOT
changed - a rejected op has no side effect.
On RANGE the bp_addr and bp_flags words report
the UNCHANGED previous values, not the request.
On OK: bp_addr is the armed address, flags 0x01.
Arming CLEARS A STALE HIT. May arm while running.

g.data-qualified-name: THE FOUR OPCODE FLOWS - TARGET_HOST only. the loopback target answers UNSUPPORTED.f_clr
g.text: 0x23 DEBUG_BP_CLR len 0
-> (OK, state, pc, bp_addr_before, bp_flags)
5 words. Disarms, clears the hit, and RELEASES
the hold. state is the RELEASED state: 1 with the
strap high, 0 with it low. pc is the PC AT THE
REQUEST - with run=0 the core re-zeroes at that
same edge, so the FOLLOWING read reports 0.
This is also how a host resumes a core that a
breakpoint stopped.

g.data-qualified-name: THE FOUR OPCODE FLOWS - TARGET_HOST only. the loopback target answers UNSUPPORTED.f_stat
g.text: 0x24 DEBUG_STATUS len 0
-> (OK, state, pc, bp_addr, bp_flags,
run, a, x, y, insn)
10 words: the common 5-word prefix plus the
architectural state, same field meanings and
widths as READ_CPU. run is the STRAP level.
ANSWERED WHILE RUNNING AND WHILE HELD.

g.data-qualified-name: THE BRING-UP TRAP - once held. the run strap is ignored BOTH WAYS.g1
g.text: THE GATE
cpu_exec = dbg_step || (run && !dbg_hold)
run is MASKED BY THE HOLD - in BOTH directions.

g.data-qualified-name: THE BRING-UP TRAP - once held. the run strap is ignored BOTH WAYS.g2
g.text: DROPPING run DOES NOT RESUME
and RAISING run DOES NOT EITHER.
A host that single-steps, or that stops on a
breakpoint, and then 're-asserts run=1 to carry
on' finds the core STILL HELD - with no fault
and nothing in the response words to explain it.

g.data-qualified-name: THE BRING-UP TRAP - once held. the run strap is ignored BOTH WAYS.g3
g.text: dbg_hold_r IS CLEARED AT EXACTLY TWO PLACES
1. reset
2. the DEBUG_BP_CLR branch
and SET by a step or by a hit. Nowhere else. So
the ONLY resume is DEBUG_BP_CLR - which also
DISARMS - or a reset.
This is a property of the debug design, not a bug.

g.data-qualified-name: THE BRING-UP TRAP - once held. the run strap is ignored BOTH WAYS.g4
g.text: THE RESUME RECIPE, if the breakpoint
is still wanted
1. DEBUG_STEP step off the breakpoint; the
hit clears, the core stays held
2. DEBUG_BP_CLR release; with run=1 it resumes
3. DEBUG_BP_SET re-arm WHILE IT RUNS
The core cannot instantly re-hit: it left bp_addr
when it stepped, and the strap resumes it from the
step's landing address. BP_SET while running
clears any stale hit, so the recipe is IDEMPOTENT.
A host that does not care about the breakpoint
just issues DEBUG_BP_CLR once.

g.data-qualified-name: THE SUBTLETY. BP_SET clears bp_en and bp_hit but NOT dbg_hold_r.c1
g.text: DEBUG_BP_CLR clears ALL THREE
bp_en, bp_hit AND dbg_hold_r

g.data-qualified-name: THE SUBTLETY. BP_SET clears bp_en and bp_hit but NOT dbg_hold_r.c2
g.text: DEBUG_BP_SET clears only TWO
bp_en and bp_hit - NOT dbg_hold_r.
So arming a core that is ALREADY HELD does
not release it, and nothing reports an error.

g.data-qualified-name: THE SUBTLETY. BP_SET clears bp_en and bp_hit but NOT dbg_hold_r.c3
g.text: WHY THAT MATTERS: the free-running hit
latch is gated on !dbg_hold_r, so an armed
breakpoint cannot produce a hit on a core that
is held and therefore not advancing. The core
sits at state 2 with bp_hit clear, forever.

g.data-qualified-name: THE SUBTLETY. BP_SET clears bp_en and bp_hit but NOT dbg_hold_r.c4
g.text: BUT DO NOT GENERALISE IT. The STEP path
is NOT gated on !dbg_hold_r - DEBUG_STEP sets
bp_hit directly from (bp_en && dbg_next_pc ==
bp_addr). So ARMING A HELD CORE IS LEGAL, and
stepping onto the armed address DOES latch
state 2 to 3. That is exactly the stop-before
flow the R2 held-core vectors use.

g.data-qualified-name: THE SUBTLETY. BP_SET clears bp_en and bp_hit but NOT dbg_hold_r.c5
g.text: WHICH IS WHY THE VECTORS OPEN WITH
DEBUG_BP_CLR. The first v10 prep re-armed a
core the v09 step had just left held; the hit
never latched and the failure surfaced as a WORD
MISMATCH INSIDE A GOLDEN RESPONSE - word 5 =
0002, want 0003 - pointing at the STATUS builder
when the cause was two opcodes earlier. Both preps
now open with BP_CLR and ASSERT the release.
THE ENCODING IS 2 BITS IN THE LOW HALF of the
word and the UPPER 14 ARE ZERO, so a host can
read it as a small integer without masking and
a swapped 2/3 encoding is still a valid-looking
word. That is exactly why it needed a vector:
a mutant swapping 2 and 3 still passes the 18
shipped R2 steps and fails only the four
held-core ones - 18/22, the four held steps and
nothing else.
bp_flags bit0 is what makes 'disarmed' and
also the only thing a host can trust after an
out-of-range BP_SET, which leaves both the
register and the reported flag untouched.
THE FREE-RUNNING LATCH AND THE STEP PATH ARE
TWO DIFFERENT PLACES, and collapsing them into
one sentence is how a host ends up encoding a
half-truth as a rule. The free-running latch
(pe_ctrl.v:692) is gated on !dbg_hold_r; the
step path (:1067) is not. A guard written from
the over-broad reading refuses to arm a held
core - which is LEGAL - and its own conformance
run is what caught it.
All four debug ops are READY-IMMEDIATE: they
are answered from registers in the request's own
CRC cycle, exactly like READ_CPU, so they emit
ZERO 0xFFFF filler words. The wait-word rule
stays what it is for the bounded reads 0x13 and
0x14 ONLY. A host must not assume every op can
return late.
NO NEW FAULT CLASS. A malformed frame (bad CRC,
bad length, bad header) answers BAD_FRAME and
has NO side effect - no step, no arming. A
sequencing refusal answers NOT_READY with no
fault, exactly like LOAD while running.
This is invisible from the response words, which
is why it is drawn with its own emphasis. It is
recorded in the contract precisely because it
costs a bring-up board a long time when nobody
has written it down - and because a host whose
MODEL declares debug_hold: true can never show
it: the model reaches the state by fiat, the
chip reaches it by traffic.
The second finding: BP_SET clears the latched
bp_hit, so re-running the pre-state prep before a
vector's SECOND step would turn state 3 back
into state 2. The prep is therefore emitted once
per VECTOR, not once per step - a golden read
does not disturb the debug state, so one call per
vector is enough. That is why the include is
generated from the step table rather than
hand-written.

BP_CLR, run=1 - RESUMES
